L262: In 14% of the statistically significant cases, cytokines exhibit an antagonistic relationship, meaning that they have opposite signaling effects on downstream targets (cite72†Fig. 3b ). For example, IL4 and BMP6 downregulate many targets induced by IL1B and TNFA (cite72†Fig. 3a and cite75†Extended Data Fig. 3a ). We also observed a similar relationship among four other cytokines: the IFNG target genes are antagonized by IL10 and GCSF but enhanced by IL27 (cite75†Extended Data Fig. 3b ).
L263: Thus, our target co-regulation analysis identified four major anti-inflammatory regulators (IL4, BMP6, IL10, and GCSF), which antagonize chiefly pro-inflammatory molecules in two groups (cite72†Fig. 3c , cite72†d ), which we referred to as the NFKB and interferon transcriptional group (cite63†Fig. 2b ).
L264: ### BMP6 Antagonizes Pro-Inflammatory Cytokine Target Genes
L265: 
L266: Previous work demonstrated that IL4 could inhibit NFKB transcription programs^{cite76†33 }, explaining the antagonistic relationship between IL4 and cytokines in the NFKB group. A previous study demonstrated that BMP6 could inhibit the CCL2 mRNA level induced by TNF^{cite77†34 }. However, to the best of our knowledge, no previous studies have reported BMP6 as an anti-inflammatory molecule that antagonizes many proinflammatory targets.
L267: Our analysis indicated that BMP6 may antagonize the effect of IL1B through down-regulating IL1B-induced pro-inflammatory chemokines, with CXCL8 and CCL2 as the most significant targets (cite72†Fig. 3a ). To validate our prediction, we first evaluated the intracellular protein levels of CXCL8 and CCL2 upon IL1B and BMP6 treatments by flow cytometry in two human lung epithelial cell lines A549 and NCI-H1299.
L268: Consistent with our data analysis, BMP6 treatment significantly inhibits the IL1B induction of CXCL8 and CCL2 (cite78†Extended Data Fig. 4a –cite78†c ). ELISA assays also indicated that levels of soluble CXCL8 and CCL2 are consistently lower in cells treated with BMP6+IL1B compared to IL1B alone (cite78†Extended Data Fig. 4d , one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value = 0.016).
L269: ### CytoSig Predicts Signaling Activities from Expression Data
L270: Since the cytokine response data in our collection reflect signaling relationships in human tissues (cite43†Fig. 1e ), we created the CytoSig model to predict signaling activities using the transcriptome profile of an input sample. The output of CytoSig is different from standard cytokine assays such as ELISA, which measure cytokine levels instead of cytokine target activities.

L455: ### CXCL8 and CCL2 detection by Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)
L456: 
L457: A549 cells were seeded in 6-well-plate at the density of 2E5 cells/well. On the next day, cells were treated with human recombinant IL1B (R&D systems, 201-LB-005, 10 ng/mL), human recombinant BMP6 (R&D systems, 507-BP-020, 10 ng/mL), and combinations of IL1B and BMP6 for 24h. Reconstitution buffers of the IL1B (PBS containing 0.1% BSA) and BMP6 (4 mM HCl containing 0.1% BSA) were used as negative controls.
